newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Bahrain tries Qatari man and woman for spying.
newsitem.headline: Bahrain tries Qatari man and woman for spying.

text.p: Bahrain on Wednesday put on trial two Qataris charged with spying, a government official said.
"Bahrain's State Security Court today started trying the two Qataris in the presence of their families," the official told Reuters.

Bahrain said on Monday the two accused, a man and a woman, had confessed before an investigating judge to spying for Doha. They were named as Fahad Hamad Abdullah al-Baker and Salwa Jassim Mohammed Fakhri.
Al-Ayam newspaper said relatives of the suspects had arrived in Manama and would attend the trial.
The case has raised tensions between Qatar and Bahrain which are locked in a territorial dispute over a group of barren islands, reefs and sandbanks controlled by Bahrain since the 1930s.
Bahrain has said it will boycott this week's Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) summit in the Qatari capital Doha, saying Qatar has behaved in an "unfriendly" manner.

Doha newspapers have said the spying charges were intended to undermine the summit and abort an initiative by Qatar's Emir Sheikh Hamad bin Khalifa al-Thani to visit Bahrain to try to persuade it not to boycott the summit.
